subsystems.name: Discrete substrate models
subsystems.role: propose a finite, rule-based structure — a cellular automaton, causal set or spin network — in place of smooth spacetime.

subsystems.name: Information formalism
subsystems.role: rewrites physical states as information and physical evolution as computation.

subsystems.name: Simulation stack
subsystems.role: runs candidate rules at sizes large enough to be compared with real physics.

subsystems.name: Correspondence tools
subsystems.role: checks whether the discrete model reproduces relativity, the Standard Model and conservation laws at everyday scales.

subsystems.name: Observational probes
subsystems.role: looks for a faint signature of discreteness in nature.

buildSteps.title: Choose a substrate and rule
buildSteps.detail: Pick a finite structure — a grid of cells, a network of qubits — and a local, reversible update rule that evolves it step by step.

buildSteps.title: Derive the continuum limit
buildSteps.detail: Show mathematically that smooth spacetime, Lorentz symmetry and known particles emerge as large-scale approximations of the rule, or identify exactly where they fail.

buildSteps.title: Encode it on hardware
buildSteps.detail: Map the rule onto tensor-network algorithms or quantum processors, because the state space grows far beyond what ordinary computers can hold.

buildSteps.title: Validate against exact results
buildSteps.detail: Reproduce cases where both the discrete model and standard physics give the same answer, to confirm the encoding is correct.

buildSteps.title: Extract a testable signature
buildSteps.detail: Find where the discrete model predicts something different — an energy-dependent speed of light, a minimum length, a bound on information density.

buildSteps.title: Search the sky and the lab
buildSteps.detail: Compare those predictions with high-energy astrophysics, clock and interferometer data; a null result tightens or kills the model.

buildSteps.title: Iterate or abandon
buildSteps.detail: If no deviation appears, revise the substrate and rule, or conclude that information is not the fundamental level.

pathway.milestone: discrete models reproduce fragments of physics — holographic codes, tensor networks, cellular-automaton interpretations of quantum mechanics
pathway.unlocks: a shared language between gravity, thermodynamics and information.

pathway.milestone: quantum simulators run small discrete space-times and lattice gauge theories
pathway.unlocks: bench-top experiments on whether geometry can emerge from a rule.

pathway.milestone: sharp, quantitative predictions for observable discreteness
pathway.unlocks: falsifiable targets for gamma-ray, neutrino and gravitational-wave observatories.

pathway.milestone: either a full correspondence to known physics or a clear refutation
pathway.unlocks: if it succeeds, a single computational description underlying all of physics; if not, the idea is retired.
